relevance_note: Two case reports of LAD-1 with homozygous ITGB2 variants: "Homozygous of two novel “likely pathogenic” missense variants ... were identified in the genomic DNA of P1 and P2".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; the JSON was assembled with a short Python script in the scratch directory and every span checked verbatim against the paper. Labels: the paper defines '(Patient #1, P1)' and '(Patient #2, P2)' and uses P1/P2 in the text ('Case 1'/'Case 2' prefix sections; 'Patient 1'/'Patient 2' head Tables 1-2 and Figure 2); P1/P2 used throughout. Table 2 has patients as columns (headers '**Patient 1**', '**Patient 2**'); Table 1 has variants as columns (c.920T>C, c.758G>A, c.262C>T). No stacked cells. Relatives: both parents of P1 are reported heterozygous carriers without stated sex ('parent of P1', 'parent of P1 2'); P2's parents are labelled father/mother from Figure 2F 'both paternal and maternal DNA'. P1's sister ('had no health issues') was neither tested nor affected, so given no row. A previously published Japanese girl (ref [16]) with necrotizing ulcers after BCG vaccination is included as 'ref [16] patient'. Inheritance: each patient is homozygous and both parents carry the variant; the enum has no biparental option, so 'inherited unspecified parent' was used. Variant pathogenicity/ACMG/type left 'not reported' for the parents' rows (D-29: about the probands' variants). CONTRADICTIONS: (1) the P1 exon 8 variant is printed 'c.920C>T' in the Abstract and Discussion but 'c.920T>C' in Results, Figure 2 and Tables 1-2; recorded as c.920T>C (Results/Table form). (2) P2: 'minimal pus with redness around the umbilical stump' vs 'Periumbilical redness with a lack of pus formation'; both recorded as observed features, checklist 'absence of pus formation' set observed on the explicit 'lack of pus formation' statement (not a direct present/absent contradiction). (3) P2 consanguinity: parents 'denied consanguinity' and Table 2 'No', but Discussion says 'consanguinity could not be excluded'; recorded 'no' as stated. Other choices: P1 had pus found at surgery, but 'absence of pus formation' left 'not reported' for P1 (presence not converted to an exclusion). P1's weight 9.5 kg (3rd percentile) not recorded as a feature (no abnormality named). 'Respiratory tract infection ... not identified in P2' used to exclude lower respiratory tract infection (broader absence). 'Normal growth parameters' used to exclude failure to thrive for P2. BCG complications excluded for both from the statement naming 'both patients'. Ages: 'They are currently six years old' (both); no age at diagnosis stated. Functional studies: 'functional studies cannot be performed at our institution', so functional evidence 'not reported'; in silico predictions in Table 1 not recorded as functional evidence. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null (paper silent).

span: Emergency tracheostomy was performed
Intravenous cloxacillin, ceftazidime, and amikacin were administered for chronic wound and soft tissue infections, resulting in good clinical responses.
Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim with itraconazole prophylaxis was initiated and a significant decline in infection was noted.
Currently, hematopoietic stem cell transplantation cannot be performed because of the unavailability of matched donors.

span: Intravenous cloxacillin and metronidazole were administered; however, her clinical condition worsened.
The intravenous antibiotics were switched to carbapenems, with some clinical improvement.
The use of intravenous gentamycin and ciprofloxacin for recurrent omphalitis improved her clinical outcome.
Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim with itraconazole prophylaxis was initiated and a significant decline in infection was noted.
Currently, hematopoietic stem cell transplantation cannot be performed because of the unavailability of matched donors.
